parameterNotes.pod: the pod the kubelet terminated; the readiness and 503 readings are its own, so the name fixes which pod of the service.
parameterNotes.node: the node whose eviction decision ended it; no series here is per node, and the name is what makes the decision somebody else's.
parameterNotes.evictionTrigger: what the eviction was decided for, which is what rules the pod and its application out; a series cannot carry whose memory was over.

groundTruth.rootCauseReason: The kubelet terminated the user-profile pod at 14:07 without letting it run a shutdown hook, acting on an eviction decision taken for a different workload on the same node. Nothing in the pod or in the application explains it: memory was well under the limit, the node's conditions were healthy, and no exception was logged because the process never received a signal it could handle. The service had no ready replica for the forty seconds a replacement took to start, and every request in that window failed.

rootCauseIndicators.description: the whole request share fails for the readiness window, which is what an evicted single-replica service looks like from outside
the replacement's time to readiness, which is the length of the outage rather than a symptom of the application

causalChain.mechanism: the kubelet acts on an eviction decision taken for another workload on the node and terminates the pod without a shutdown hook
the service is left with no ready replica for the forty seconds the replacement takes to start, so every request in that window fails

evidenceCheckpoints.description: every request fails for the outage window -- the sentence that says the whole service was gone rather than degraded, and the reading that could not be declared before the sampling noise was held to the unit's range
the replacement's time to readiness, which is the length of the outage; `>=` because the text gives forty seconds as the wait, not as a bound
the node's own condition never left ready, which is what rules the node out as the thing that broke

remediation.action: give the workload a disruption budget and spread its replicas across nodes, so an eviction decision taken for one workload cannot leave a service with no ready replica
terminate with a grace period that lets the process run its shutdown hook, so a deliberate eviction and an unplanned kill do not look identical from inside the container

query: The user-profile pod was terminated at 14:07 and every request 503'd until a replacement was ready forty seconds later. What is the root cause, and why is the node not it?
